value: real COSMIC v3.6 SBS3 weight vector (96 contexts)
rationale: P06R2 fix: the 96-context shape mutations attributable to the "HRD process" are distributed across, when building SIMULATED_mutation_catalogs.tsv. Was ARBITRARY (v1/v2's _make_shape, C>T-favored) until P08 found it was less similar to real SBS3 (cos=0.688) than to real SBS5 (cos=0.802) -- not actually SBS3-shaped. Now the real vector itself, extracted live from the installed, GATE1.json-verified SigProfilerAssignment 1.1.5 package (COSMIC version 3.6, PROTOCOL.md §5.4's pinned bundled default). No hand-tuning.

value: real COSMIC v3.6 SBS5 weight vector (96 contexts)
rationale: P06R2 fix, paired with hrd_shape above -- same extraction, same file, SBS5 column. SBS5 chosen (unchanged from the original design's intent) as a common, ubiquitous background/clock-like process real cosine-similar to SBS3 (0.7928), which is exactly the confusability property that made this feature scientifically interesting to test in the first place.

P06R2 acceptance floor: hrd_shape is constructed to BE the real COSMIC SBS3 vector exactly, so a live re-extraction from the installed package must round-trip to this vector at essentially 1.0 cosine similarity (floor allows only floating-point noise, not a "chosen to pass" tolerance). Checked by scripts/check_p06r2_acceptance.py against a fresh docker-side extraction, not at simulate.py runtime (see SIMULATION_SPEC.md §3.1).

P06R2 acceptance band, centered on the real, fixed COSMIC v3.6 SBS3-vs-SBS5 cosine similarity (0.7928, computed from COSMIC_SBS3_SBS5_v3.6_reference.tsv -- there is no independent literature source for this exact number beyond COSMIC's own reference matrix, which is authoritative here). Guards against "fixing" the shape defect in the opposite direction (an unrealistically separable target) -- checked at simulate.py runtime in build_signature_shapes().

NEW (v2): given a sample's direction draw is NOT WT-lost, the split between RETENTION and VARIANT_LOSS. Not Z-linked (an engineering simplification -- only the 3 headline evidence features described in PROTOCOL.md §6 are Z-linked); a simple, disclosed, class/arm-independent constant.

NEW (v2, DEFECT 1): given a loss direction (WT-lost or variant-lost), the probability the mechanism is a genuine deletion (n_t=1) rather than copy-neutral LOH. Weighted above 50% because large-scale copy-number loss is the more commonly reported real-world second-hit mechanism, and because DEFECT 1 specifically requires robust deletion-type representation; not tuned to hit any specific downstream count (DRAWS_PER_GRID_CELL was the parameter iterated for that).
